statements.label: theo:universality_L2_full
statements.scope_notes: PARTIAL 2026-09-08 -- but the WEAK HALF IS NOW PROVED FROM THE PAPER'S OWN HYPOTHESES, end to end. `weaklyUniversal_of_kernel` takes exactly: pi_star a Markov kernel, nu a finite measure, nu.bind pi_star = nu (the paper's nu_B pi_star = nu_B), ||pi_star||_{L^p -> L^p} <= C, summable L^p-mixing, p != inf -- and concludes WeaklyUniversal. NO OPERATOR IS HYPOTHESIZED ANYWHERE ON THE PATH: the density action P_star f = d((f.nu) pi_star)/d nu is CONSTRUCTED (`densityAction`, via `bindDensity` = ((nu.withDensity f).bind kappa).rnDeriv nu) and packaged as a CLM. Absolute continuity of (f.nu)pi_star w.r.t. nu is PROVED from invariance alone, not assumed -- so the body's claim that 'invariance makes the density action well defined' is exactly right and nothing else is needed. Sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated. Chain of files: Core/Kernel (kernel -> operator) -> Core/Flow (the mean projection and the intertwining identities, derived) -> Core/Mixing (Step 1) -> Core/Universality (Step 2) -> Core/UniversalityLp (Step 3). WHAT REMAINS, both disclosed and unchanged: (i) Pi is the MEAN projection, not proved to be the projection onto ker(Id - P_star) -- ergodicity has moved into the summability hypothesis, and `eq_meanProj_of_invariant` proves that is where it went, since under summable mixing against the mean projection every invariant L^p element is a.e. constant; (ii) STRONG universality at p = +inf is NOW CLOSED (`stronglyUniversal_of_kernel_top`, from the same kernel hypotheses), and so is the cross-p transfer AT ONE PAIR (`stronglyUniversalAt_of_kernel_Lr`): the realizing outflow lies in every L^r(nu) and the defect is exactly zero there. The compatibility that makes the transfer possible is a theorem, not a hypothesis, for the paper's own object -- Core/Kernel's `densityAction` is defined pointwise on functions and is p-free, so the CLMs at two exponents are induced by one function-level map. WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVED, and is a different claim: strong L^r-universality of the L^r FAMILY for r < inf. The cross-p clause delivers a realization in L^r for a pair whose densities are in L^inf; a pair merely in L^r is out of reach by this route, since S theta need not be essentially bounded and the construction's eta would not exist. The paper does not claim otherwise -- its p = inf clause is stated under p = inf hypotheses. Also open: non-vacuity at p = inf, since no kernel satisfying the whole p = +inf bundle is exhibited. The boundedness hypothesis cannot be dropped -- it is false for some Markov kernels, and the paper says so three times (universality.tex:6-9, :27-29, proofs.tex:36). A non-vacuity witness is provided (`isBoundedDensityAction_id`) so the hypothesis is not empty.

statements.label: lem:adjoint
statements.scope_notes: PARTIAL 2026-09-08, sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated -- FINITE state space, disclosed. All three items on a general kernel over a Fintype with a general NON-NEGATIVE invariant lambda (not tied to a marked graph), so Balance/Lift and the DB block get a reversal layer to build on: (1) existence, Markov-ness a.e. and the characterizing identity lam x * R x y = lam y * A y x, with lambda-a.e. uniqueness; (2) lambda is invariant for the reversal, the flip identity -- the relation is SYMMETRIC, which is the whole content -- and the a.e. involution; (3) mutual adjointness on L^2(lambda), each density action is the other's function action, the contraction, and the operator norm EXACTLY 1 as an `IsLeast` with attainment at lambda. Two things came out better than the paper's phrasing, both stated as such: EXISTENCE IS UNCONDITIONAL -- the identity holds even where lambda(x) = 0, because invariance forces lambda(y)A(y->x) = 0 there, so only Markov-ness of that row degrades (`IsMarkovOn` vs `IsMarkov`); and the INVOLUTION NEEDS ONLY lambda(x) != 0, not lambda(y) != 0, since lambda(x) != 0 = lambda(y) forces A(x->y) = 0. No lambda > 0 is assumed anywhere; 'lambda-a.e.' is `lam x != 0`. `Graph.reversal`, `pdens` and `qact` are all `rfl`-equal to the general definitions, so every theorem applies to the graph objects verbatim. NOT DONE: the general Polish case. Items (1)-(2) are reachable at this Mathlib pin (`Measure.condKernel`, `eq_condKernel_of_measure_eq_compProd`, `Measure.compProd`, `Measure.fst_map_swap`); item (3) is obstruction 2 in full, and ONE PIECE IS GENUINELY MISSING FROM MATHLIB: a kernel-Jensen `(int u d kappa_x)^2 <= int u^2 d kappa_x`, which would have to be built from `inner_mul_le_norm_mul_norm` on L^2(kappa x).

It is now a THEOREM. `hasDerivAt_loss_ipL2`: for every direction d, the directional derivative of L at mu is <lossGradDensity ... | d>_{L^2(lambda)}; and `lossGradDensity_unique`: no other function represents those derivatives. So the three disclosures collapse, and each file now carries a dated amendment pointing here. The general preconditioner nu_G = varpi.lambda is covered (`hasDerivAt_loss_ipL2_precond`), so it is NOT a restriction. The paper's own second-order expansion is transcribed verbatim (`ratio_expansion`, `remainder_abs_le`). CROSS-CHECKED NUMERICALLY, not merely proved: `twoState_hasDerivAt_loss` evaluates the theorem on prop:nonlinear_freezing(2)'s two-state chain with g = (x-1)^2 and gets 9/16, computed by hand two ways -- off the perturbed ratios and off the gradient side -- before the Lean was run. statements.label: theo:gd_diffusion_full
statements.scope_notes: PARTIAL 2026-09-12, sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated -- the first Lean this statement has had. THE EXPANSION IS CLOSED WITH AN EXPLICIT c(eps) = 2 K eps, K = 2 C_4 + C_5 the paper's own constants (gd_diffusion_display, on Expansion.lean's gradient_expansion). IT IS PROVED UNDER A C^3-TYPE TAYLOR BOUND ON g', NOT UNDER THE PAPER'S C^2 HYPOTHESIS, whose c(eps) -> 0 is non-effective and is NOT stated here; neither statement implies the other. That is a disclosed collision between rule 1 (never state more than the paper proves) and rule 3 (constants are explicit formulas), resolved toward the shape theo:local_convergence_full Step 1 actually consumes, which is the only consumer either display has. The weak form is reachable -- replace the Taylor remainder by the modulus of continuity of g' at 1 -- and is left unstated deliberately. THE FLOW SENTENCE IS NOT STATED: linHess is exhibited as an operator and the expansion proved, but 'the linearization of the gradient flow is hdot = -H h' is not made, and no ODE appears. THE 'IN PARTICULAR' CLAUSE is closed as two OPERATOR identities under detailed balance (Core.IsReversalPair lam K K): linHess = g''(1) (I-P)^2 for w = 1, and H phi = g''(1)(1-beta)^2 phi at an eigenmode P phi = beta phi. Reversibility is needed for BOTH halves, not just the first -- confirmed, and the paper states it. 'Each eigenmode DECAYS at rate' is the flow reading and is not made. Finite state space. CONSTANTS, re-derived independently before comparison: C_g, C_5 and K match the paper exactly; C_4's 3 M_3 is reached with 8/3 M_3 and (r-1)^2 <= 4 eps |A h_perp| with 32/9, so the paper's printed values are valid but not sharp, and are used as printed. |1/(1+h)^2 - 1| <= 4 eps is valid and not sharp at eps = 1/4 (true sup 7/9 against 4 eps = 1); it is the STEP the paper routes through, (2 eps + eps^2)/(1-eps)^2 <= 4 eps, that is exactly tight at eps = 1/4, so the constraint eps <= min(a,1)/4 is conservative rather than wrong. Two hypotheses Lean needs explicitly and the paper has implicitly: 0 <= wsup and 0 <= a, underivable on an empty state space. NON-VACUITY, checked by hand in exact rationals BEFORE the Lean and agreeing on the first run: on the two-state chain with g = (x-1)^2, h = (1/5,-1/5), D = (175/432, -175/288), H h_perp = (2/5,-2/5) as linHess_eigen independently predicts at beta = 0, and ||E||^2 = 805093/37324800 against the bound 16/15.

statements.scope_notes: PARTIAL 2026-09-08, sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated. THE CONTINUOUS DISPLAY IS CLOSED, both conjuncts: Pi h_t is conserved and ||h_t - Pi h_t|| <= e^{-rho t} ||h_0 - Pi h_0||, on any real inner-product space, by Gronwall. `inner_ge_of_mixing` supplies the coercivity from Core.Mixing, giving rho = c/B-hat^2 in the paper's shape. THE LINEARIZATION IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A DERIVATION, and is disclosed in four places: H := g''(1) A-dagger M_w A comes from theo:gd_diffusion_full, which is bucket D, so the decay is stated for a curve satisfying hdot = -H h with H carrying exactly three properties -- Pi self-adjoint, Pi H = 0, and the coercivity -- and rho is any constant satisfying it rather than g''(1) w_min / B-hat^2. NOT assumed and not needed: H self-adjoint, H >= 0 as an operator, Pi idempotent, rho > 0. THE DISCRETE DISPLAY IS CLOSED TOO (2026-09-12, GFNBounds/Balance/Discrete.lean, sorry-free, axiom-swept): along h_{k+1} = h_k - eps H h_k the component Pi h_k is conserved and ||h_k - Pi h_k|| <= (1 - eps rho)^k ||h_0 - Pi h_0||. The paper's step condition eps <= (4 g''(1) ||w||_inf)^{-1} enters as the QUADRATIC-FORM bound <x,Hx> <= Lam ||x||^2 with eps Lam <= 1 -- weaker than the paper's operator-norm bound, hence a stronger theorem; ||A|| <= 2 => ||H|| <= 4 g''(1) ||w||_inf is NOT derived, A not being present. IT COSTS TWO HYPOTHESES THE PAPER'S DISCRETE SENTENCE DOES NOT NAME, both true of the paper's objects: H SELF-ADJOINT and Pi IDEMPOTENT. Self-adjointness is load-bearing, not cosmetic -- the route the proof sentence names (the energy method, through ||Hx||^2 <= ||H|| <x,Hx>) delivers only the factor sqrt(1 - eps rho), and the printed 1 - eps rho needs 0 <= I - eps H <= (1 - eps rho) I on the invariant subspace ker Pi, proved here without spectral theory by Cauchy-Schwarz for a symmetric semi-definite form (norm_apply_le_of_symm_bounds). Note also that ||Hx||^2 <= ||H|| <x,Hx> is itself false without self-adjointness (a rotation has <x,Hx> = 0, ||Hx|| = ||x||), and that H >= 0 does not imply symmetry over a REAL space. eps rho <= 1 is carried, not derived. Tightness: on E = R with H = 2.id, Pi = 0, eps = 1/4, rho = 2, h_k = 5 (1/2)^k, the two sides are EQUAL at EVERY k and sqrt(1 - eps rho) = 0.707... is strictly weaker (scalar_discrete_check). STILL NOT DONE: the lem:lift_mixing transfer to the FM and DB losses. Cross-checked for non-vacuity and for the exponent: on E = R with H = 2.id, Pi = 0, h_t = 5 e^{-2t} a genuine solution, the two sides are EQUAL at t = 1 -- so the exponent is exactly rho, not rho/2 or 2 rho. statements.label: prop:frozen_unstable_full
statements.scope_notes: PARTIAL 2026-09-08, sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated. THE FM HALF IS CLOSED, in all four conjuncts: 0 <= F_0 <= F, the loss vanishes at F + F_0 = F*, and it is strictly positive at F. Two things came out better than the brief expected. (a) The inflow mu_F = lambda - eps.d(gamma) is not merely non-negative but >= lambda/2 > 0, and the proof does not go edgewise: eps.d(gamma)(v) = sum_u eps.1_gamma(u->v) <= sum_u (1/2)F*(u->v) = lambda(v)/2, using row-stochasticity of pi_back. So `eq_smul_invProb` applies unchanged and no uniqueness among SIGNED invariant vectors is needed. (b) The cycle is HYPOTHESIZED as a `MarkedCirculation` structure -- non-negative, a circulation, non-zero, vanishing at s_0 and s_f -- rather than constructed, which dodges a combinatorial layer and STRENGTHENS the statement: every 1_gamma of the paper is such a circulation and the converse fails. Non-vacuity of the eps interval is `exists_admissibleEps` with an explicit witness. statements.label: prop:no_distant_equilibrium
statements.scope_notes: PARTIAL 2026-09-08, sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated. CLOSED: item (1), the mass identity, in all three of its conjuncts -- the mass equals int g'(r)(1-r)(dnu/dmu) dlambda, it is <= 0, and it is 0 iff mu is balanced -- plus `balanced_of_critical`. Proved once and shared between the two labels. Finite state space, disclosed: every downstream use is on a finite graph and the general case would need obstruction 2 merely to say what Q phi is. THE BOUNDARY, and it is the point of the file: `D := Q phi - r phi` is a Lean DEFINITION, never derived. Identifying it with the gradient of L_{g,nu} is theo:first_variation_full's job, which is bucket D and not formalized -- so what is certified is the mass of THAT EXPRESSION, and the words 'every critical point is balanced' are conditional on that identification. 'Critical' is read as D = 0, not as 'the first variation vanishes in every admissible direction'. Three further weakenings in the safe direction: ergodicity is NOT assumed (only lambda-invariance, so uniqueness of the balanced flow is not certified), lambda need not be a probability, and K need not be row-stochastic. One thing came out stronger than the paper: r > 0 is DERIVED from invariance plus positivity rather than hypothesized as 'essentially bounded away from 0 and infinity'. ITEM (3) IS NOW CLOSED TOO -- both the pointwise inequality |g'(x)(1-x)| >= delta^2/2 (each of its four elementary bounds a separate named lemma) and the integrated display, the latter stated over ANY far set and with d nu/d mu >= c_0 abstract, hence more general than the paper's. It needs lambda(S) = 1, which this file carries and MassIdentity does not -- the paper says 'since lambda is a probability measure' at proofs.tex:809, so nothing is wrong, but the hypothesis is genuinely used there and not in item (1). ITEM (2)'s FIRST HALF IS NOW CLOSED as well: `ipL2_lossGrad_self` proves int D u dlambda = 0 as a BARE IDENTITY -- no invariance of lambda, nothing about g -- and `nrmL2_const_of_flow` turns it into the invariant sphere ||u_t|| = ||u_0|| along the gradient flow, which is the paper's 'the gradient flow preserves ||u_t||'. NOT DONE: item (2)'s Lyapunov half (the mass strictly increases, Cauchy-Schwarz on the sphere, LaSalle) and the convergence half of the dichotomy, which need a gradient-flow / LaSalle layer. ITEM (2)'s LYAPUNOV HALF IS NOW CLOSED (2026-09-12, GFNBounds/Balance/MassAscent.lean, sorry-free, axiom-swept): the mass int u_t dlambda is differentiable along the flow with derivative -int D dlambda >= 0 (hasDerivAt_mass_flow, mass_monotone_flow), strictly positive off balance (mass_deriv_pos_off_balance), and bounded on the invariant sphere by ||u_0|| with equality exactly at a constant density (mean_le_nrmL2_iff_const -- Cauchy-Schwarz against 1 WITH its equality case, which the library did not have). TWO DISCLOSURES. (a) That equality case needs u >= 0: the paper's 'equality if and only if u is constant' is false as a statement about L^2 (at u = -1 the two sides are -1 and 1), and densities supply the missing hypothesis which the sentence does not name. (b) 'BALANCED => CONSTANT' IS ERGODICITY AND IS FALSE under this layer's `Invariant K lam` alone -- K = Id on two states makes every lambda invariant and EVERY u balanced -- so the paper's 'whose unique maximizer is the balanced flow' is certified only on a marked graph (mass_ascent_lyapunov_graph, through Graph.eq_smul_invProb); the paper itself is fine, since prop:no_distant_equilibrium hypothesises an ergodic (S-hat, lambda, T), and the gap is between that hypothesis and the weaker one MassIdentity.lean carries. ITEM (3)'s ENTRY TIME is closed as well: exists t_1 in [0, L(mu_0)/c(delta)^2] with every ratio within delta, c(delta) = w_min lambda_min^{3/2} delta^2 / (2 ||u_0||) explicit (cDelta, entry_time), which reproduces proofs.tex:813 exactly. Delivered as an EXISTENCE of an entry time rather than the paper's forward-invariant reading 'after time at most L(mu_0)/c(delta)^2 all ratios are within delta': the budget argument bounds the total off-band time, and permanence is theo:local_convergence_full's, which is how the paper's own assembly uses it. STILL NOT DONE: LaSalle, the boundary blow-up / compactness step, and the convergence half of item (3).

statements.label: prop:morozov_rate
statements.scope_notes: PARTIAL 2026-09-08, sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated -- 1159 lines. ITEMS (1) AND (2) CLOSED. The headline finding: **prop:morozov_rate does not need a Markov chain.** Every chain object in it is the unique solution of a square linear system on V, and all three are solvable and uniquely so from what Graph/Setting.lean already proves: E(sigma | X_0 = .) is `IsHitExp`, E(sum_{n<sigma} f(X_n)) is `IsPoisson`, the killed occupation measure is `IsGreen`, and N := g + 1_{s_0} + 1_{s_f}. Existence is LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective; uniqueness is a maximum principle walked down to s_0 along `breach_all`. Item (1) then says `visits` is P-invariant of total mass 2 + sigma_bar, and an invariant SIGNED measure of an irreducible chain is a multiple of lambda. Item (2)'s ||u||_inf <= sigma_* ||f||_inf survives the characterization, as a comparison: phi := c.u - u_f vanishes at s_0 and is superharmonic off it because c - f >= 0 is exactly the slack. ONE DEVIATION, in the safe direction: the paper closes item (2) by transferring coercivity from I-Q to I-P via 'their restricted inverses have the same norm', an operator-adjoint argument, i.e. obstruction 2. That is routed around by a duality pairing -- <h,h> = <h,(I-Q)w> = <(I-P)h,w> -- which uses only pointwise adjointness and no operator norm, so the paper's 'h - u is Q-harmonic hence constant' step is unnecessary and is not formalized. NOT DONE: item (3), which is a claim about how theo:db_stable_frozen, theo:local_convergence and theo:global_dichotomy consume the constant -- none of the three is in this library, and rho_sigma is likewise not stated. The leveled-graph witness is stated in its B-hat_sigma half only (`Leveled.bsigma_le`); the B-hat = +inf half needs the operator-norm layer, so the file exhibits a finite B-hat_sigma where the paper says B-hat is infinite, without certifying that B-hat is infinite.

statements.label: cor:global_lojasiewicz
statements.scope_notes: CLOSED 2026-09-08 in BOTH displays, sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated -- finite state space, disclosed. The static inequality kappa.L <= ||D|| and its squared form came first (Balance/Lojasiewicz.lean); Balance/Flow.lean then closed the flow layer and with it the second display, L(mu_t) <= (L(mu_0)^{-1} + kappa^2 t)^{-1}, with kappa the paper's EXPLICIT formula and not an exists-C. The route: `hasDerivAt_loss_flow` proves -Ldot = ||D||^2 -- provable rather than assumable now that theo:first_variation_full makes D the gradient -- and `lojasiewicz_integrated` integrates the differential inequality. NO EXISTENCE THEOREM IS NEEDED: every claim is 'for any curve satisfying the ODE', which is how the paper's proof reads. A hypothesis was also REMOVED: the sphere constraint ||u_t|| = ||u_0||, assumed in the static file, is a CONCLUSION along the flow (`nrmL2_const_of_flow`, from the bare identity int D u dlambda = 0), so ||u_0|| in kappa is literally ||d mu_0 / d lambda||. 2026-09-12 (GFNBounds/Balance/MassAscent.lean): the flow form is now usable at the paper's own constant. `global_lojasiewicz_flow'` states it with L_0 literally L(mu_0), discharging both hypotheses `Flow.global_lojasiewicz_flow` carries -- hL0 by antitonicity of the loss along the flow (loss_antitone_flow, lossVal_antitone_flow) and hpos by lojasiewicz_integrated_nonneg, which needs only 0 <= L(0) rather than positivity throughout. LIBRARY DEFECT FOUND AND REPAIRED THE SAME DAY: `Flow.global_lojasiewicz_flow`'s hL0 was quantified over ALL of R (`forall t : R, L(mu_t) <= L0`) while its sibling hpos was correctly ranged over 0 <= t; since the loss is antitone the paper's L0 = L(mu_0) gives the REVERSE inequality below 0, so the hypothesis was undischargeable at its intended instantiation and `global_lojasiewicz_flow'` had to re-derive the statement rather than apply it. hL0 now reads `forall t, 0 <= t -> ...`; it was used exactly once, in a context where 0 <= s was already in scope and discarded, and the repair was verified by ELABORATED TYPE rather than by source diff. kb/0022 records the class. The re-derivation in MassAscent is left standing: it is proved, and rewriting a verified file to route through the repaired theorem buys nothing.

statements.label: theo:universality_graphs
statements.scope_notes: CLOSED 2026-09-08 in ALL THREE ITEMS, sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated. (1) irreducibility, existence, uniqueness and positivity of lambda, and lambda(s_0) = lambda(s_f) -- Mathlib v4.31 has no finite-chain Perron-Frobenius, so the paper's Levin-Peres citation was PROVED. (2) the frozen-backward family is exactly the ray f_out = c.lambda with pf the lambda-reversal, both directions. (3) cutting the wrap edge gives exact flow matching: `fmDefect_eq_zero` at every internal state, `termFlow_eq_target` (F_term = Z.pb(s_f -> .)), `sum_initFlow` (mass Z), and `residuals_eq_zero`. Two disclosed choices. (a) The forward half of (2) assumes of pi_-> only that its rows sum to 1, never non-negativity -- the paper's Theta asks for a kernel, and dropping an unused hypothesis strengthens the statement; the converse proves both halves for the reversal, so no member is lost. (b) The paper lets f_out* vanish and calls the policy 'immaterial' there; rather than adding a side condition, `outflowStar_mul_fwdStar` proves the identity the flow-matching computation actually consumes -- f_out*(u) . pi_->*(u->v) = e(u->v) -- UNCONDITIONALLY, since f_out*(u) = 0 forces e(u->v) = 0. Not a corner case: on s_0 -> a -> s_f the unique internal state has f_out* = 0 exactly. NOT DONE, and named: the sampler clause of item (3) and the closing paragraph rest on theo:sampling_theorem, which the paper quotes from bengio2021flow; there is no trajectory space in the file and no hypothesis carrying it, because without a model of the sampler such a conditional would merely restate its own hypothesis. Nor is the bridge to Core's `StronglyUniversalAt` built -- see the obstruction note.

statements.label: rem:loop_closure_necessary
statements.scope_notes: CLOSED 2026-09-08, sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated -- and by a shorter route than the paper's. The marginal step is the paper's: summing the invariance identity over u gives sum fout = sum fout - fout(s_0), so fout(s_0) = 0, with no sign condition. But instead of the paper's Doeblin argument (leak to s_0 within #V steps, iterate), the zero PROPAGATES FORWARD along the edges of G: fout(u) = sum_v fout(v) pb(v->u) with fout >= 0 forces fout(v) = 0 at every out-neighbour of a vanishing vertex, since pb(v->u) > 0 there and v != s_0 because s_0 has no in-edge; PathConnected reaches every vertex from s_0. No kernel powers, no minorization, no extra hypothesis.
